questions.question: Doubles and triples:

options.text: Turn easily because of their centers of gravity.
Are harder to turn than smaller commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are harder to turn than smaller commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because of their size, doubles and triples cannot turn suddenly. They need extra care when turning to prevent rollovers.

questions.question: Trailers built before 1975:

options.text: Do not need to have spring brakes.
Cannot be driven on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not need to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: One way to avoid jackknifing is to:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Drive smoothly to reduce jackknifing risk. Watch the road ahead so you have time to react to hazards.

questions.question: Skids caused by acceleration can usually be fixed by:
questions.explanation: Release the accelerator to correct acceleration skids. On very slippery surfaces, you may also need to push the clutch in.

questions.question: Compared to other commercial vehicles, combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and they:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Managing space is especially important when operating a combination vehicle.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping air once the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Changing lanes too quickly can cause:

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that causes a rollover.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that causes a rollover.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect from rearward amplification can cause a rollover when you change lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle.

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by:
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure gets too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:

options.text: Clean and free of oil or grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean and free of oil or grease.
questions.explanation: Brake pads and shoes must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: For a vehicle with power steering, check the hoses for:

options.text: Whether they are connected to the battery.

questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look specifically for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Steer with one hand to keep the other hand free.

questions.explanation: Always follow the posted speed limit in work zones. Slow down if the road or weather is bad. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen.
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast.
A valve that prevents the trailer from being released by accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: Which statement about doubles is true?

options.text: They are easier to drive than singles.
They are less likely to roll over than singles.
They are less likely to jackknife than singles.
They need more time to react to hazards than singles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more time to react to hazards than singles.
questions.explanation: Doubles must be driven smoothly to avoid jackknifing and rolling over. Look far ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: What should you do if a trailer begins to skid?
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This lets the wheels grip the road again. Once they grip, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: When coupling a triple trailer rig, which trailer should you couple first?

options.text: The trailer closest to the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer closest to the cab.
questions.explanation: Couple the trailer closest to the cab first. Then connect the second and third converter dollies and trailers in order.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control knob?

options.text: Air goes to the emergency lines.
The air system disconnects from the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air goes to the emergency lines.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control knob to send air to the emergency lines. This knob is red and eight-sided.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions need double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral. Then release the clutch, let the engine speed match the road speed, push in the clutch again, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: What happens if there is no air pressure in the trailer brakes after coupling?

options.text: There will be no air in the cab.
The load will not be supported properly.

questions.explanation: After coupling trailers, check that air reaches all the brake lines. If air does not flow all the way to the back, the brakes will not work.
